items.summary: HEAVY CEILING-PATH STEP (B) — re-enable the trained value head at MCTS leaves (r12-selfplay-gate-throughput.md item 4, DEFERRED to R111). Root mechanism behind the iter-2-peak-then-rot ceiling: in rollout-leaf mode the trained value head is never used at gate/self-play (backend/src/sim/mcts.ts:552-555), so the loop has NO improving signal feeding back into MCTS across iters. Re-enabling the value head at leaves would give the loop a positive gradient toward ground-truth z (terminal outcomes), letting visits ratchet SHARPER instead of softer across iters. COST: changes the learning targets, breaks the R110 A/B chain (R110-W6 production claim 96-d 0.6479 is rollout-leaf-based); any new run establishes a new baseline. NEW EVIDENCE 2026-05-21 from R16-P2 C8b/C8c: v3.2 + value-head-leaf has now been DIRECTLY TESTED in two configurations — C8b iter-0 0.3798 (raw v3.2 init) and C8c iter-0 0.3481 (init from C8 iter-0 0.5955 ckpt). Both regressed below 0.40; C8c WORSE than C8b despite stronger init falsifies the 'trained-ckpt unlocks vhleaf' hypothesis. Consistent with R13.W8 v3.0 vhleaf history (0.452→0.404→0.340→0.380). HYPOTHESIS FALSIFIED: 'value head needs better STATE REPRESENTATION to support vhleaf' is dead — slot-token state didn't fix it. REMAINING HYPOTHESIS: 'value head needs better CALIBRATION' — which is exactly what value-head-data-program Stage 1 tests (regress-to-rollout-means on the W6 corpus, gated by R14 crossover probe at val_mse<=1.10*W3-floor AND pearson>=0.7).

items.summary: Relabel MCTS bleeds the shared AsyncLocalStorage RNG into the game's deterministic trajectory. Surfaced as a secondary finding in chunk 5i (runs/R16-TD-3a-prod-corpus-400sim-rulebot/flip-analysis.json:recipe_invariant_check): rule-bot-mirror at --mcts-simulations 400 produced 4233 rows vs 4196 at 100 sims (state-identical intersection 63.8% of 100-sim rows) despite --selection baseline being deterministic — only 63.8% of (seed,modelSide,step) keys carried identical legalActions across sim counts. Root-cause hypothesis: relabel MCTS consumes the shared AsyncLocalStorage RNG via the global random() proxy in frontend/src/game/engine/core/random.ts (storageProvider.get()?.next() ?? Math.random()), so additional sims perturb the game's RNG before the next baseline move. Invalidates the chunk-5h 'deterministic row-by-row diff at 4x sims' design; salvageable for the chunk-5i verdict (state-identical subset still yielded a 95% CI well below the 30% LIVES threshold) but invalidates any future sim-count A/B comparison until fixed. NOT on the critical path of active research — the active research line (chunks 5g+5h+5i) already concluded candidate-1 dies; this is forward-looking infra.
items.next_action: DEFERRED, not blocking. Fire only if a sim-count A/B becomes load-bearing again (e.g. reframed step 1 chooses a sim-count axis). Two fix sketches: (a) isolate relabel MCTS in its own RNG context — wrap runMctsRelabel in a separate AsyncLocalStorage.run with a forked RNG so sims do not consume the game's RNG token stream; or (b) two-pass design — generate the corpus once at low sims, then re-relabel only policyTargets (no game re-run) at higher sims against the recorded GameState. Option (b) also makes sim-count sweeps trivially cheap (no extra game wall-clock). Pointer: docs/ai-research/progress/r16.md sub-§ 'Step 2 verdict (chunk 5i)' secondary finding.

items.summary: G1+G2 LANDED 2026-05-22 (ort cuda feature flag + Device::{Cpu,Cuda} enum + SessionGuard splitting CPU-Mutex from CUDA-UnsafeCell + --device/--cuda-device-id flags on sim-eval-gate). ABI: ort 2.0.0-rc.12 + ORT 1.22.0 CUDA EP loads clean (cudnn.so.9 + ancillary nvidia libs from training/.venv via LD_LIBRARY_PATH). G4 FALSIFIED at n=200 workers=16 on R110-W6-repro/iter-0/policy.onnx (sims=100, leaf=rollout, rollout-steps=200): CUDA wall 55.18s vs CPU 10.77s = 5.12× SLOWER (gate requires ≥1.5× faster). Strength agreement gate PASSED: |wl_cuda-wl_cpu| = |0.5007-0.4957| = 0.005 < 0.02 envelope; modelWinRate 0.570 vs 0.565. Per-side wilsonLower agreement also within 0.025: player 0.4623 vs 0.4426, opponent 0.4821 vs 0.4920. Root cause matches the scoping risk: at --leaf rollout the per-leaf heuristic rollout (200 TS-equivalent steps) is hundreds× heavier than the one ONNX call it replaces, so moving inference to GPU adds H2D/D2H latency and per-call kernel-launch overhead with no compensating compute win. CPU per-call ORT runs ~10-100us in-process; GPU per-call ~5-15ms incl. transfers — at 100 sims × 200 games the GPU overhead dominates. STRENGTH AXIS (gpu-fed-stronger-mcts.md) is the right lever from here: GPU buys higher sims at acceptable wall, not lower latency at fixed sims.
